# Results — Study 667 (Negative Volume Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Norman Fosback's (1976) **Negative Volume Index**: cumulate the index's return only on
days trading volume FALLS versus the prior day (freeze it otherwise); whenever the
resulting NVI line sits above its own 1-year (255-session) EMA, Fosback claimed "the
odds favor a bull market" with **96% reliability**. Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints
`d65c4c93a643` (^GSPC) / `2f5662f8e29a` (SPY).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape (signal) | yfinance daily **^GSPC** OHLC + Volume (19,244 rows), 1950-01-03 → 2026-06-30 — the first session Yahoo! reports non-zero S&P 500 volume |
| Real tape (tradable proxy) | yfinance daily **SPY** total-return OHLC + Volume (8,411 rows; `auto_adjust=True`), 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30 |
| Indicator | NVI (base 1000, cumulates return only on volume-down days) and its 255-session EMA — Fosback's own "1-year" span |
| Statistics | Wilson interval on conditional bull-year probabilities; a 20,000-draw label-shuffle placebo on the annual test; Welch *t* (naive) and Newey-West HAC *t* (lag = horizon — the overlap-robust number) on 21/63/252-day forward returns; HAC *t* on the daily active spread of the costed timer; a 2,000-draw circular-shift placebo |
| Execution / one documented lag | NVI/EMA state is fully known at the close of day *t* (that day's price AND volume); every forward-return and every timer position uses that state to predict/hold from the close of *t+1* onward — a single shift, applied once, everywhere |
| Costs | timer: one-way × NAV per leg (0 / 5 / 10 bps swept); long-only, no borrow |
| Data quirks (named) | ^GSPC is a **price index — no dividends, no adjustment concept**; its Volume is Yahoo's index-level vendor tape, a proxy for the NYSE's 1976 official composite tape Fosback used, not the tape itself. SPY Close is **total-return** (dividends folded in via `auto_adjust=True`); its Volume is the ETF's own consolidated tape. Building NVI on each series' *own* reported volume (rather than a separate breadth feed) is the standard modern implementation (StockCharts, MetaStock) and the one the brief specifies — a named proxy limitation, not a silent one |

No survivorship: ^GSPC and SPY are an index and a single diversified ETF, not
cross-sectional survivor panels.

## The headline — Fosback's own annual framing, replicated

NVI/EMA state read at each calendar year's final close predicts the **following**
year's realized return (a scheduled, zero-incremental-look-ahead entry at a state
already fully known) — the same year-over-year bull/bear framing Fosback used with
1941–1975 NYSE data. "Bull year" = realized return > 0.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| sample | **74 calendar years, 1952 → 2025** |
| P(year up \| NVI>EMA at prior year-end) | **70.3%** (n=37, Wilson [54.2%, 82.5%]) |
| P(year up \| NVI<EMA at prior year-end) | 75.7% (n=37, Wilson [59.9%, 86.6%]) |
| P(year up) — **unconditional base rate** | **73.0%** (n=74, Wilson [61.9%, 81.8%]) |
| gap (NVI>EMA minus the unconditional base rate) | **−2.7 pp** |
| label-shuffle placebo (20,000 draws, same duty cycle) | observed gap −2.7 pp vs placebo mean +0.00 pp (sd 5.20 pp) → **p = 0.790** |

Fosback's "96% reliable" figure does **not** appear on 74 years of S&P 500 data — on
this replication the NVI>EMA conditioning doesn't even match the market's own
unconditional tendency to have an up year (73.0% of all 74 years were positive, simply
because equities drift up most years), let alone beat it. The point estimate is
actually **lower** when NVI says "bull" than when it says nothing at all, and a
20,000-draw placebo shows a gap this size (or bigger) happens **79% of the time** under
pure random labeling with the same duty cycle. The famous number is a base-rate
artefact, and on this sample it doesn't even clear the base rate itself.

## Higher-power daily cross-check — the overlap trap, named and corrected

Forward 21/63/252-trading-day returns split by regime, on the full 19,244-session
^GSPC tape. The **naive Welch *t*** treats every overlapping day as an independent
observation — a textbook trap that manufactures huge *t*-values purely from sample
size; the **Newey-West HAC *t*** (lag = horizon, Hodrick-style) is the number the
desk's REAL bar is actually judged against.

| horizon | mean fwd return, NVI>EMA | mean fwd return, NVI<EMA | naive Welch *t* | **Newey-West *t*** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 trading days | +0.877% (n=9,513) | +0.611% (n=9,454) | +4.24 | **+1.18** |
| 63 trading days | +2.490% (n=9,471) | +1.961% (n=9,454) | +4.98 | **+0.84** |
| 252 trading days | +10.018% (n=9,282) | +8.435% (n=9,454) | +6.83 | **+0.60** |

The naive Welch *t* climbs as high as **+6.83** — exactly the kind of number that gets
quoted in NVI folklore write-ups — but it is measuring ~9,000 heavily overlapping
windows as if they were independent trials. Once the overlap is corrected the honest
*t* **never exceeds 1.18** at any horizon: indistinguishable from noise everywhere.
Hit-rates by regime (informational only — the same overlap inflates their Wilson
intervals too, so treat the 74-year annual test above as the credible, correctly-sized
version): 21d on 63.7% vs off 59.4%; 63d on 69.8% vs off 63.2%; 252d on 78.0% vs off
70.5%.

## Third axis — the costed long/flat timer (SPY, tradable proxy)

Long when SPY's own NVI (built on the ETF's own reported volume) is above its 255-day
EMA, cash otherwise; one execution lag (position formed on the close of *t* earns
*t+1*); Sharpe figures are net and, with rf = 0 here, net = excess-of-cash.

| cost (one-way) | Sharpe net (B&H) | CAGR net (B&H) | active spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | 0.563 (0.647) | +8.76% (+10.83%) | −0.816 | **−2.38** |
| 5.0 bps | 0.560 (0.647) | +8.69% (+10.83%) | −0.840 | **−2.44** |
| 10.0 bps | 0.557 (0.647) | +8.62% (+10.83%) | −0.865 | **−2.50** |

Signal ON (long) **93.2%** of 8,411 sessions, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30; **41 switches
in 33.4 years** (1.23/yr) — costs are immaterial (gross ≈ net) because turnover is so
low; max drawdown net **−57.7%** vs buy-and-hold **−55.2%**.

**The timer doesn't just fail to add value — it loses to buy-and-hold at a
statistically significant HAC *t* = −2.44.** A 2,000-draw circular-shift placebo (real
position path, shifted against returns) confirms it: the observed gross spread
(−0.816 bps/day) is **worse than 98.5% of random re-timings of the same path**
(*p* = 0.985) — the rule's actual calls carry negative information, not positive.

### Robustness — sample-half split (SPY, own NVI, cost = 5 bps)

| half | window | Sharpe net (B&H) | active spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| H1 | 1993-01-29 → 2009-10-07 | 0.265 (0.455) | −1.681 | **−2.45** |
| H2 | 2009-10-08 → 2026-06-30 | 0.855 (0.872) | −0.329 | −0.81 |

The underperformance is significant in the first half and fades but never flips sign
in the second — not a single-regime artefact.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic tape: a sticky hidden two-state regime (mean duration ~130 sessions)
where the "accumulation" state both (a) makes volume MORE likely to fall day-to-day
(62% vs a neutral 50%) and (b) carries a TUNABLE extra drift `edge` — the literal
Fosback mechanism (quiet days cluster exactly when informed accumulation is
happening). `edge = 0` removes the drift link while keeping the quiet-day clustering,
so any detection there would be a pure false positive.

| world | Newey-West *t* (252d horizon) |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge=0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.11** (sd 0.94), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted `edge=+0.4` (seed 667) | on +72.5% vs off +39.5%, Welch *t* = +28.64, **Newey-West *t* = +2.90** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up cleanly on a planted "quiet days
precede drift" effect. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support
of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Fosback's own annual framing shows **zero** improvement over the
  unconditional base rate (70.3% vs 73.0%, gap **−2.7 pp**, label-shuffle *p* = 0.790)
  on 74 years of S&P 500 data — the 96% figure does not replicate, and the point
  estimate is even slightly negative. The higher-power daily cross-check never clears
  **t ≥ 2** once the overlapping-return trap is corrected (Newey-West *t* tops out at
  **+1.18** at 21 days); the naive Welch *t* (up to +6.83) is exactly the illusion the
  desk's HAC bar exists to catch.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A long/flat SPY timer built on the rule **loses to
  buy-and-hold**, not merely fails to beat it: active spread **−0.84 bps/day at HAC
  *t* = −2.44** (net, 5 bps costs), gross barely different (**t = −2.38**, costs are
  not the story), and a circular-shift placebo shows 98.5% of random re-timings of the
  same path do better. Robust in direction across both sample halves.
- **"NVI>EMA = ~96% bull-market odds?" — BUSTED.** Even measured exactly the way
  Fosback measured it, conditioning on NVI's regime state adds nothing over simply
  knowing equities drift up most years — the headline number is a base-rate artefact
  that, on this 74-year replication, doesn't even reach the base rate itself.
